required_features: One wizard player character controlled with mouse-directed click/hold movement, with the cursor also serving as the aiming/targeting reference for spells
Charged Fireball (tap for quick shot, hold to charge, costs mana, restricts movement while charging)
Frost Field (temporary area that heavily slows enemies; cast/mana side owned by Wizard Combat Agent, slowdown application/restoration owned by Enemy Pursuit Agent)
Force Wave (short-range radial knockback with a long cooldown)
Mana pool with slow regeneration after a brief post-cast delay
Melee Enemy (runs at wizard, attacks at close range)
Ranged Enemy (keeps distance, fires slow telegraphed shot, requires line-of-sight/occlusion checks; never appears without at least one Melee Enemy in its encounter)
Sealed Door: open by holding 5 uninterrupted seconds; movement or damage cancels and resets progress
Sealed Door: close-and-lock after crossing, restoring a small fixed amount of health; once locked it cannot be reopened, unlocked, or crossed again
Sealed Door: durability/breaking under sustained pursuer attack when the player waits too long; a broken door stays open permanently and is not a player return path
Cross-room pursuit: enemies follow the wizard through open doors as persistent objects (not new spawns), carried forward across rooms
Hard cap of 15 active enemies at once; new-encounter activation is delayed/reduced first when persistent pursuers plus a new encounter would exceed the cap
Health persists across the whole run (does not regenerate or reset between rooms except via door-lock recovery)
Death and restart: reaching zero health restarts the entire floor from the beginning

One handcrafted, continuous 2.5D isometric dungeon floor with five connected spaces (Ruined Entry, Bone Archive, Chapel of Ash, Lower Vault, Final Room), authored primarily with Unity Isometric Tilemaps for floors/walls plus SpriteRenderer prefabs for doors/props/characters, viewed with a fixed isometric camera
Essential feedback: door banging/shaking/cracks/durability indicator, Force Wave cooldown visibility, and other core status feedback (health, mana, door progress)
Windows build of the finished game with no runtime AI/network dependency

current_state.implemented_summary: Only a single self-contained 'Door Prototype' feature exists under Assets/NoSafeCircle/DoorPrototype/. It provides: a CharacterController-based player driven by WASD keyboard input (PlayerMovement.cs) rather than the GDD's mouse-directed click/hold movement; a basic PlayerHealth component with TakeDamage and a Damaged event but no regeneration, cross-room persistence logic, or death/restart handling; a DoorInteractable component implementing only the 'hold 5 seconds to open, cancel on move/damage' behavior (no closing, locking, health-restore-on-lock, durability, or breaking); a DoorInteractionUI showing a prompt and progress-fill bar; a DebugDamageControl that lets a developer manually trigger player damage for testing (explicitly a debug/test affordance, not a combat system); and an Editor script (DoorPrototypeSceneBuilder.cs) that procedurally builds one small test room out of primitive Unity geometry (a Plane floor, two Cube walls, a Cube door visual, a Capsule player visual) with no Tilemap, no isometric camera framing beyond a single fixed test-room camera, and no room layout resembling any of the GDD's five named spaces. No spell scripts, no mana scripts, no enemy/AI scripts, no NavMesh usage, and no Tilemap assets exist anywhere under Assets/. Play Mode and Editor tests exist only for this door-opening/cancel behavior and for scene-builder UI wiring, not for any other GDD system.
files_reviewed: Glob of Assets/**/* (confirms only Assets/Scenes/SampleScene.unity, Assets/Scenes/DoorPrototype.unity, Assets/InputSystem_Actions.inputactions, and the DoorPrototype folder exist; no other gameplay scripts, Tilemap assets, enemy scripts, or spell scripts anywhere under Assets/)

candidate_goals.name: Mouse-Directed Click/Hold Player Movement
candidate_goals.description: Replace or extend PlayerMovement.cs so the wizard moves via mouse click-to-destination or hold-to-steer-toward-cursor over the gameplay plane, with the cursor established as the shared aiming/targeting reference, matching the GDD's Move-and-Aim specification instead of the current WASD-only scheme.
candidate_goals.implementation_scope: Assets/NoSafeCircle/DoorPrototype/Scripts/PlayerMovement.cs (rework input handling to raycast from the mouse cursor onto a ground plane and drive the existing CharacterController toward that point); minor exposure of an aim-point property other systems could later read.
dependencies: PRE-EXISTING: PlayerMovement.cs and its CharacterController-based movement pipeline
PRE-EXISTING: existing test-room scene/camera built by DoorPrototypeSceneBuilder.cs for manual verification
CREATED-IN-GOAL: mouse-to-ground-plane raycast/projection logic
candidate_goals.resource_acquisition_reasoning: This is a code-only input/movement change; it requires no external art or generated resource, so PixelLab is not relevant here and resource acquisition readiness is high by default.
systems_unlocked: Cursor-based spell aiming reference for future Fireball/Frost Field/Force Wave targeting
GDD-accurate movement feel for later playtesting
candidate_goals.risk_and_size: Small, low-risk change confined to one existing script; main risk is correctly projecting the cursor ray onto the gameplay plane given the test room's non-final camera angle.
candidate_goals.reasoning: Fixes a real, evidenced divergence between the current WASD implementation and the GDD's required Move-and-Aim scheme. High readiness on every axis, but its unlock value is bounded because WASD movement already lets the door prototype be exercised end-to-end today — this candidate refines an already-functioning system rather than standing up a wholly missing one.

Scoped to single-room chase-and-attack only, not multi-room door pursuit.

dependencies: PRE-EXISTING: Player GameObject/CharacterController as a chase target (Assets/NoSafeCircle/DoorPrototype/Editor/DoorPrototypeSceneBuilder.cs BuildPlayer)
PRE-EXISTING: PlayerHealth.TakeDamage() as the damage entry point (Assets/NoSafeCircle/DoorPrototype/Scripts/PlayerHealth.cs)
PRE-EXISTING: Floor/Walls primitive geometry to bake a NavMesh over (DoorPrototypeSceneBuilder.cs BuildFloor/BuildWalls)
CREATED-IN-GOAL: baked NavMesh, NavMeshAgent component/config, enemy prefab, detection/attack state logic
ACQUIRED-IN-GOAL (optional, not blocking): PixelLab-generated directional enemy sprite art for later visual polish

PixelLab is relevant for eventual 4/8-directional enemy sprite art and could supply it later, but that acquisition is not required to implement or test this candidate now, and importing/rigging that art (sorting, animation wiring) would remain separate integration work regardless.
systems_unlocked: First functional enemy/combat threat in the project (currently zero enemy code exists anywhere)
A live damage source to validate PlayerHealth beyond the current debug-only damage trigger
Foundation for later Frost Field/Force Wave interaction testing

No enemy code of any kind exists under Assets/, making this the largest true gap among coherently-sized candidates, and it is directly testable today using pre-existing Player/PlayerHealth/floor geometry without needing any new external resource.

selected_goal.name: Melee Enemy Chase-and-Attack Prototype
selected_goal.description: Add a Melee Enemy prototype (NavMeshAgent-driven) that detects the player within a radius, chases using a baked NavMesh on the existing test-room floor, and deals damage via PlayerHealth.TakeDamage() on contact, with a basic attack cooldown — scoped to single-room chase-and-attack only.

selection_reason: Among the five candidates, this one has the highest unlock value at comparably high readiness: it is the only candidate that stands up an entirely absent required system (zero enemy/AI code exists anywhere under Assets/), whereas the other four candidates all extend or refine systems that already have partial real implementation (movement, doors, health). Its prerequisites are genuinely ready today — the Player GameObject, PlayerHealth.TakeDamage() damage entry point, and Floor/Walls geometry to bake a NavMesh over all already exist from the door prototype — and no external resource blocks prototyping it, since a primitive placeholder enemy (consistent with the project's existing primitive-art style) is sufficient to validate chase-and-attack behavior. Its prototype_readiness is high (fully testable today in the existing single test room with a baked NavMesh), but its integration_readiness is low, since no isometric floor, encounter design, or the other required systems (spells, mana, door pursuit) exist yet to validate the real multi-room tactical context described in the GDD. This tradeoff is acceptable because every reviewed candidate currently has low integration_readiness against the real game context — none of the five spaces or the isometric presentation layer exists yet — so integration_readiness does not meaningfully discriminate between candidates at this stage, while prototype-testable unlock value does, and this candidate maximizes that unlock value by creating the game's first live combat threat rather than incrementally polishing an already-partial system.
dependencies: PRE-EXISTING: Player GameObject/CharacterController target (built by DoorPrototypeSceneBuilder.cs BuildPlayer)
PRE-EXISTING: PlayerHealth.TakeDamage() damage entry point (Assets/NoSafeCircle/DoorPrototype/Scripts/PlayerHealth.cs)
PRE-EXISTING: Floor/Walls primitive geometry to bake a NavMesh over (DoorPrototypeSceneBuilder.cs BuildFloor/BuildWalls)
CREATED-IN-GOAL: baked NavMesh, NavMeshAgent-based enemy prefab, detection radius, attack-cooldown state logic
ACQUIRED-IN-GOAL (non-blocking): PixelLab-generated directional enemy sprite art for later visual polish
evidence: Glob of Assets/**/*.cs returns only 7 gameplay scripts, 2 test scripts, and 1 editor scene-builder script, all under Assets/NoSafeCircle/DoorPrototype/ — no enemy, AI, spell, or mana script exists anywhere.

PlayerHealth.cs (Assets/NoSafeCircle/DoorPrototype/Scripts/PlayerHealth.cs) already exposes a public TakeDamage(float amount) method and a Damaged event, providing a ready-made damage entry point for an enemy to call.
DebugDamageControl.cs is explicitly documented in its own source comment as 'Testing/demo affordance only, not a combat system,' confirming there is no real combat/damage source in the project today.

DoorPrototypeSceneBuilder.cs BuildPlayer() creates a Player GameObject with CharacterController, PlayerHealth, PlayerInteractionController, and PlayerMovement components at Assets/NoSafeCircle/DoorPrototype/Editor/DoorPrototypeSceneBuilder.cs lines 156-183, giving a ready-made chase target.
DoorPrototypeSceneBuilder.cs BuildFloor() (lines 108-114) and BuildWalls() (lines 139-154) create primitive Plane/Cube geometry suitable as NavMesh-bake source geometry.

GDD Section 3 'Required Enemy Roster' explicitly lists Melee Enemy as a required feature ('Runs at the wizard and attacks at close range... Prevents long stationary casts and becomes dangerous in groups').
GDD Section 3 'Required Scope' bullet list explicitly includes 'two enemies' among the required scope items.

GDD Section 5 'Runtime Implementation' states 'Unity navigation and finite-state components will control enemy movement, pursuit, attacks, and target loss,' confirming NavMesh-based enemy AI is the intended technical approach this candidate follows.

rejected_high_priority_alternatives.name: Mouse-Directed Click/Hold Player Movement
rejected_high_priority_alternatives.reason_rejected: This is a real, evidenced gap (PlayerMovement.cs uses WASD via Keyboard.current with no mouse/cursor input at all) and scores high on every readiness axis, but it refines a movement system that already works well enough to exercise the existing door prototype end-to-end. It does not, by itself, unlock any new gameplay system the way standing up the project's first-ever enemy does, since no spell exists yet to make cursor-based aiming meaningful.

rejected_high_priority_alternatives.name: Sealed Door Close-and-Lock with Health Restore
rejected_high_priority_alternatives.reason_rejected: Also high-readiness and low-risk, since it extends the only already-partially-implemented required system in the project. However, its core rationale — 'locking a door against pursuers' — has no real stakes while zero enemies exist anywhere under Assets/; the pursuit and breach-pressure half of the door loop is meaningless without a pursuer object, so implementing the enemy first creates more real, testable value per the GDD's own design pillars ('safety is always temporary... because of monsters left alive').
